answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by implementing a scarce-slot auction where identities must bid for limited slots that increase in cost with each new entrant. Each new identity must secure endorsements from established peers, boosting its credibility while also raising costs. As competition grows, the bidding price escalates exponentially, often reaching over $10,000 for multiple identities. To succeed, an attacker must invest heavily, akin to trying to establish a harbor in the tundra while battling relentless storms at the wharf, which only amplifies their financial strain.
